prompt: Review an unseen regulated AWS workload from organization and identity through VPC, compute, data, observability, quota, recovery and cost; adapt after the reviewer changes one major constraint without using an AWS account.
deliverables: User-operation, data-class, demand, SLI, SLO, RPO and RTO contract.
Organization, OU and account model with governance, audit and break-glass ownership.
Human and workload identity map with every relevant policy boundary.
Regional request and state path across DNS, network, entry point, compute and data.
EC2, ECS, EKS and Lambda comparison with a justified selection.
Immutable artifact, IaC plan review, progressive rollout and rollback contract.
S3 or RDS consistency, encryption, key, retention, backup and restore design.
Burst and AZ-loss capacity model including quota, stock, subnet and dependency limits.
User-centered telemetry, alert, incident and recovery-verification design.
Cost-unit model, rejected alternative, migration risks and exact local cleanup.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer supplies an unseen workload and changes Region, recovery, traffic, residency, team-skill or budget constraints after the first design.
No AWS account, credential, CLI, SDK, API, provider download, terraform apply, public endpoint or paid resource is used.
A sanitized pre-generated Terraform plan may be reviewed but cannot be treated as deployment or capacity evidence.
Every diagram labels scope, state owner, failure domain, trust boundary and operating owner.
Capacity calculations include steady state, burst, one-AZ loss, scaling delay, quotas, subnet IPs and downstream limits.
One broad IAM fix, one unjustified Kubernetes design and one unsafe cost reduction are explicitly rejected.
Recovery evidence specifies point selection, restore order, application validation, achieved RPO/RTO and failback.
Reviewer observes changed-constraint reasoning, delayed recall, uncertainty labels and cleanup.
